solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Kilo — measure of weight — taken the wrong way as measure of speed

indicators.note: taking something the wrong way here means the word for the weight is read backwards

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A muddled reading of a kilogram as if it measured velocity.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends kilo and weight belong together; 'taken the wrong way' is the reversal signal, and the definition sits at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a nautical unit of speed, one nautical mile per hour.

clue.text: What inspired potter may do for the big finale?

definitions.text: What inspired potter may do for the big finale?

parts.words: What inspired potter may do for the big finale?
parts.note: a potter at the wheel might turn a star shape as a showpiece; the phrase also means the headline act of a show

explanation.surface: A creative ceramicist plans a showstopping last piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The potter seems to be a craftsperson at the wheel, turning a star; the phrase really names the main attraction of a variety bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the principal act or performance, the highlight that tops the bill.

clue.text: Drinking companion possibly overturned computer

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the combined pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: pot is drink, as in a pot of ale or potting at the bar
a pal is a friend or companion

explanation.surface: A fellow boozer knocked a computer over.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer used on the knees.

clue.text: Composer limits note in endless chord

parts.note: pales are boundaries or limits, as in beyond the pale

indicators.note: in signals that the note goes inside the shortened chord
endless means the last letter of the chord word is dropped

parts.note: a triad is a three-note chord

explanation.surface: A musical instruction about a chord being cut short and bounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts TRIAD to TRIA, and 'in' puts N inside it to make TRINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was the great Italian Renaissance composer of sacred music.

clue.text: Problem about performance involving new private room

indicators.note: about means the problem word goes around the rest

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: involving means the performance word wraps around the letter for new

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A dilemma over a new show staged in a private room.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'involving' works first on the performance and new, then 'about' wraps the arithmetic problem round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a secluded private retreat, such as an inner study.

clue.text: Left supporting introduction of Socialist game

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed underneath, so the left word comes after
the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: The political left backing a Socialist's opening move in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Sport is a general word for a game or athletic pastime.

clue.text: Sweet version of the comical look, nothing less

indicators.note: a version of the phrase is a reworking of its letters
less means a letter is left out of the reworked phrase

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A sugary take on a funny face, with nothing missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of THE COMICAL LOOK, which contain an extra O; 'less' removes that O.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk chocolate is a confection, and sweets are confections in British usage.

clue.text: Ringing of bell, say, in jolly style?

parts.note: a la, the French borrowing, means in the style of, so 'in ... style' gives it
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: Ringing a bell in a cheerful manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like a cheerful adjective but is a Royal Marine; 'in ... style' gives A LA, so the phrase reads in the style of a marine.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a warning signal, of which a ringing bell is an example.

clue.text: A lot of drink? Certainly a quantity of drink

indicators.note: a quantity of a word, only part of it, means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: mead is a drink made from honey
sure means certainly, as a reply

explanation.surface: Someone asking for plenty to drink and being told yes, a fair amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quantity of' means only part of the honey drink, its last letter gone; the question mark flags the definition as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is a standard serving of spirits, and a large one is plenty to drink.

clue.text: Sailor behind increasingly reduced artillery weapon

indicators.note: behind means the sailor word comes after the other piece
reduced means the final letter is clipped off

parts.note: increasingly is more and more, so more
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor falling ever further back while a big gun is cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortar is a short-barrelled gun firing shells at high angles.

clue.text: University student returned article published about Protestant movement

indicators.note: returned means the two letters for university and student are read backwards

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver
the is the definite article
ran means published, as a paper runs a story

explanation.surface: A college student going back to an article printed about a church movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutheran means relating to the church founded on Martin Luther's Reformation teachings.

clue.text: Enliven competition, bagging runs? It'll set you on your way

definitions.text: It'll set you on your way

indicators.note: bagging means holding inside, so the runs letter is tucked in

parts.note: stir up means to rouse or enliven
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a cup is a competition, as in the FA Cup

explanation.surface: Livening up a cricket tournament by piling on runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup cup is a farewell drink handed to a rider already mounted, before departure.

clue.text: I try working with energy absorbing upcoming crucial theory in physics

indicators.note: absorbing means taking the crucial word inside
working means these letters are set to work in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: upcoming in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: vital means crucial

explanation.surface: A scientist labouring with energy on a key theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' looks like the scientist at work but shuffles I TRY and E; 'upcoming' reads the crucial word upwards in this down clue, and 'absorbing' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Relativity is Einstein's theory of space, time and motion.

clue.text: I'll have foremost of tickets on display?

definitions.text: I'll have foremost of tickets on display?

indicators.note: the foremost of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: out means on show or displayed

explanation.surface: A ticket seller boasting about showing off the best seats.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by a ticket tout, who keeps tickets on show for touting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tout sells tickets for events at inflated prices, typically outside venues.

clue.text: Presently exhausted by party?

parts.note: all in means exhausted
a good time is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone shattered at the moment from partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presently' looks like 'now', but means in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means eventually, at the right moment, which is the older sense of presently.

clue.text: Wind reasonable, force dropping, not high

indicators.note: dropping means the letter for force falls to the end of the reasonable word

parts.note: fair means reasonable
F is the symbol for force
low means not high

explanation.surface: A weather report: a moderate wind, dropping in strength and low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' moves the F of FAIR down to its end, giving AIRF.
explanation.definitionFit: Airflow is a current of air, which is wind.

clue.text: Buds that will be damaged in cascade of soil

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of the fodder are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Young shoots spoiled under a landslide of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust bath is a bird's practice of flinging dry earth over itself, a shower of soil.

clue.text: Perseverance? Old King has it

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A former monarch with staying power.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, the dogged persistence of perseverance.

clue.text: Punch — way to constrain constant complainer

parts.note: a cross is a punch in boxing

indicators.note: to constrain means to hold inside, so the path wraps the constant

parts.note: a path is a way
C is a mathematical constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A boxing blow used to restrain a perpetual whinger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' suggests Punch and Judy, but here it is a boxing blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspatch is a bad-tempered, grumbling person.

clue.text: Comedian accepting a new rumour

indicators.note: accepting means taking the other letters inside

parts.note: a card is a joker or comic person

explanation.surface: A comic taking on a fresh piece of gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is an unfounded story or false report.

clue.text: Coastal location with unknown birds

parts.note: a cove is a small bay on a coast
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A seaside inlet with mysterious birdlife.
explanation.definitionFit: A covey is a small flock of game birds such as partridges.

clue.text: Careless person I start to avoid in European country

parts.note: a sloven is an untidy, careless person

indicators.note: start to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A slob trying to start dodging something in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is a nation in central Europe, formerly part of Yugoslavia.

clue.text: Judge appearing in Times almost exhausted? Crikey!

indicators.note: appearing in means placed inside the following pieces

parts.note: by means times, as in two by three

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is lost

parts.note: over means finished or exhausted

explanation.surface: A judge, nearly worn out, appears in a newspaper, prompting an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means multiplied by; 'almost' clips the last letter of the exhausted word, and 'appearing in' puts the judge inside.
explanation.definitionFit: By Jove is a dated exclamation of surprise, much like crikey.

clue.text: Spaniard having month around University or America

indicators.note: around means the month goes round the letter

parts.note: Jan is short for January

explanation.surface: A Spanish man whose month involves a college or the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: Either route works: JAN around U, or JUN (June) around A for America; 'or' offers the choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Juan is a common Spanish man's name, typifying a Spaniard.

clue.text: Quality server lacking current

indicators.note: lacking means without the current letter

parts.note: a waiter serves at table
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A good waiter without any current trends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quality' fits the phrase 'of the first water', meaning of top grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Water means the grade of clarity of a gem, hence quality or standard.

clue.text: Sure, Tay at sea exhibits it

definitions.text: Sure, Tay at sea exhibits it

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The Scottish river Tay, where it meets the sea, has a broad tidal mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is a Scottish river with a famous wide estuary at Dundee.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary is the tidal mouth of a river where it meets the sea.
